text.text:
Behind the Rocca Sillana, near an area called "Sorripi," you can explore the Buche Fiorentine, two fascinating natural caves of significant geological interest. Located in a formation of sandy limestone, these caves are situated just a few meters apart from each other and represent the largest subterranean cavities in the area. The first cave features a slippery entrance of about 30 meters and houses colonies of bats, while the second cave, with a vertical entrance of over 15 meters, extends for more than 50 meters and boasts impressive stalactitic and stalagmitic formations.

text.text:
The Pieve dei Santi Filippo e Jacopo, located in the western part of Montecastelli Pisano, was built in 1186 by Bishop Ildebrando Pannocchieschi of Volterra. It is one of the few complete examples of Romanesque religious architecture, featuring a facade of squared stone blocks and three large arches.
Inside, it houses a painting by Cosimo Daddi (1585-88) depicting the Immaculate Conception with Saints Anthony, Ursula, and Francis. The Madonna is shown in prayer, supported by cherubim, while the Saints, in a contemplative posture, invite the faithful to participate. The scene also includes the Tree of Knowledge and a serpent with bat-like wings.

text.text:
Montecastelli Pisano is a medieval village situated on a hill at an altitude of 503 meters, 16 km from Castelnuovo Val di Cecina. It is surrounded by the Cecina River to the east and the Pavone Stream to the west.
The village retains a medieval appearance with narrow streets, cramped alleys, covered passages, and stone houses arranged in concentric circles. The main roadways lead to the parish church and the tower. The remains of the ancient walls are still visible, including a well-preserved southern entrance gate with a rounded arch made of squared stone blocks.

text.text:
Leaving Montecastelli towards Castelnuovo Val di Cecina, you will find a striking Etruscan hypogeum known as the "Buca delle Fate," dating back to the 6th century BC. This rectangular cavity, carved into limestone and supported by a central pillar, features tunnels leading to the niches that once housed the bodies of the deceased. Although lacking furnishings, the tomb displays numerous early Christian symbols, indicating that it was used as a refuge by the faithful during Roman persecutions.

ev1724676367985.description: Leaving Montecastelli towards Castelnuovo Val di Cecina, you will find a striking Etruscan hypogeum known as the "Buca delle Fate," dating back to the 6th century BC. This rectangular cavity, carved into limestone and supported by a central pillar, features tunnels leading to the niches that once housed the bodies of the deceased. Although lacking furnishings, the tomb displays numerous early Christian symbols, indicating that it was used as a refuge by the faithful during Roman persecutions.

text.text:
The settlement of Montecastelli Pisano is dominated by the imposing keep-tower of the Pannocchieschi family, currently privately owned and not open to the public. The tower was built in 1215 by Bishop Pagano dei Pannocchieschi to protect the adjacent church, which was destroyed by the militia of the Commune of Volterra in 1219 and rebuilt in 1343 by Bishop Felice Belforti.
The stone tower has a square shape, with a slightly sloped base that separates it from the vertical wall. The entrance is located on the first floor, and the remains of a rounded arch window at the top suggest that the upper floors were used for residential purposes.

text.text:
"Il Poggio" is a cultural center located in Montecastelli Pisano, founded by Philipp Bonhoeffer. The center offers a variety of modern facilities for conferences and events, including rehearsal rooms with pianos, a concert hall with professional recording equipment, and an outdoor courtyard for events. The facilities are designed to host cultural and educational activities, providing an environment that fosters creativity and innovation.
"Science and Music" is a specific project realized within Il Poggio that combines science and music. This project provides a stimulating environment where musicians and scientists can collaborate, share ideas, and inspire each other through masterclasses, concerts, scientific brainstorming sessions, and musical instrument testing. Specifically, this project studies the sound waves emitted by musical instruments and investigates how these waves are perceived by the ear and subsequently processed by the brain.

text.text:
Montecastelli Pisano has a history dating back to 1114 when Ruggero of the Counts of Bergamo, Bishop of Volterra, received some property on that hill. The castle was built in 1202 by Bishop Ildebrando Pannocchieschi and Guasco, the progenitor of the Counts Guasco della Rocca, who divided the domain among themselves. In 1204, the inhabitants submitted to the Commune of Volterra, but the Bishop retained control until the end of the 13th century when the Commune took the castle by force, destroying several structures, including the keep, the palace, and the bishop's tower.
At the beginning of the 14th century, the Commune of Volterra acquired portions of the castle and the seigneurial rights of the Pannocchieschi and Guasco counts, and in 1318 obtained the bishop's portion of the lordship from Bishop Ranieri Belforti. The dispute was resolved in the mid-century with the cession by Bishop Filippo Belforti. In 1319 and 1337, the inhabitants swore allegiance to Volterra, but in 1370 they submitted to Florence, only to return under Volterra's control in 1381. At the end of the 18th century, Montecastelli was incorporated into the community of Castelnuovo Val di Cecina.

text.text:
The Museum of Rural Civilization in Montecastelli Pisano, inaugurated in 1985, is dedicated to documenting the agricultural and craft activities of the Val di Cecina. The collection, composed of donations from local residents, includes work tools dating from the 19th century and the first half of the 20th century. These tools encompass items used by carpenters, cobblers, blacksmiths, and tailors, as well as molds for producing tiles and bricks, scales, and various implements such as forks, shovels, scythes, and spades.
